title: Saga Dawa
hook: the Tibetan month of the Buddha's birth, awakening and passing, when good deeds are said to multiply
tomorrow: Year two close: his own words

segments.voice: Yesterday: Magha Puja and its three short verses. Your line: the heart of it.

The circuit around the old city of Lhasa is already full by sunrise. People walk it clockwise, spinning prayer wheels, murmuring mantras. Some stop every few steps to bow all the way to the ground. Along the route, people sit with open bowls, and pilgrims press small notes into bowl after bowl. It's not a single holy day, and it isn't only in Lhasa. It's a whole month. In Tibet, this is Saga Dawa.
screen: `A CIRCLE AROUND LHASA.` → `BOWLS ALONG THE ROUTE.` → `A WHOLE MONTH.`

segments.voice: Saga Dawa is the fourth month of the Tibetan calendar, usually around May or June. Dawa means month, or moon. Saga is the name of a star group, a lunar mansion the full moon sits near that month. So: the month of Saga. What makes it holy? In Tibetan tradition, the Buddha's birth, awakening and passing are all remembered in this month, with the big day on the full moon, called Saga Dawa Duchen, the great occasion. You may remember Vesak, where Theravada lands keep all three on one full moon. This is a Tibetan cousin of that idea, with its own dates and customs: in Tibet, the birth is often marked on a different day, earlier in the month. Then comes the part people talk about most. Tibetan teachers say that during Saga Dawa, the effect of any action, good or harmful, is multiplied many times over; on the full moon, some say, by a hundred thousand. Some teachers put the stress on attention: a month when every small act is said to count for more, so people make them on purpose. They walk the pilgrim circuits, around the Jokhang, around Lhasa, and some walk all the way around Mount Kailash. Some families give up meat for the month. Some buy animals destined for slaughter and set them free. And they give, especially to anyone with a bowl out on the pilgrim route. A note pressed into a bowl, an animal set free, a day without meat: in Saga Dawa, each small act is treated as large.
screen: `DAWA, MONTH. SAGA, A STAR.` · `BIRTH, AWAKENING, PASSING.` · `GOOD DEEDS MULTIPLIED.` · `CIRCLES, FREED ANIMALS, GIFTS.` · then, large: `THE HOLY MONTH.`

segments.voice: Let three people or causes come to mind, one at a time: someone near you who could use something, someone you pass every day and never really see, a cause you've meant to help and haven't. Hold each for a few breaths and ask quietly what you could give: time, money, food, attention, a letter. No need to decide everything; just let one gift become clear.
Saga Dawa. The fourth Tibetan month, holding the Buddha's birth, awakening and passing, when good deeds are said to multiply. Today's word.
Your line: the holy month. A month for giving on purpose. See you for the last day of year two.

howItsDone: During Saga Dawa many Tibetan Buddhists walk pilgrim circuits such as the Lingkhor around Lhasa, give to beggars and monasteries, free animals, keep vegetarian, recite mantras and make offerings, especially on the full moon of Saga Dawa Duchen.

chat.says: Why do Tibetans give so much during Saga Dawa?
options: In that month, the effect of any action is said to multiply many times.
Because giving is not allowed in the other months of the Tibetan year.
Because Saga Dawa remembers only the Buddha's own gifts to beggars.

Saga = the lunar mansion corresponding to Sanskrit Vishakha (Pali Visakha), linking to the name Vesak: please confirm.

Dates: in Tibetan tradition the birth is often kept on the 7th of the 4th month and awakening/passing on the 15th; schools differ. Script says 'often marked on a different day, earlier in the month'. Confirm.
Multiplication of merit: commonly given as 100,000 times on Duchen (some sources say ten million); script hedges with 'some say'. Confirm.
Customs (Lingkhor circuit, Jokhang Barkhor, Kailash kora, tsethar animal release, vegetarianism, giving to beggars): please confirm wording.
